q: As per ACS-11 (para 7(a)(i)), the maximum portion of a works contract that may be sub-contracted is:

options.A: 50% of the contract price

q: Which statement about sub-contracting under ACS-11 is correct?

options.A: The contractor must execute at least 60% of the work directly with own personnel, sub-contractors' credentials are not counted in bid evaluation, and the contractor remains wholly responsible for sub-contractors
options.B: The contractor may sub-contract the entire work
options.C: Sub-contractors' credentials decide the bid ranking
options.D: The Railway deals directly with sub-contractors for payment

q: As per ACS-11 (Annexure VI), the bid-capacity threshold has been reduced from advertised value more than Rs 20 crore to:

options.A: More than Rs 50 crore

q: Pre-award punitive action under ACS-11 para 18(2) includes:

options.A: Only a warning letter
options.D: Forfeiture of bid security, calling off negotiations, and rejection/exclusion of the bid

q: Post-award punitive action under ACS-11 includes:

options.A: Cancellation of contract, recovery of compensation, forfeiture of securities/PGs, and recovery of advances with interest

q: Under ACS-11, banning/debarment of a contractor is for a minimum period of:

options.A: 6 months
options.D: 1 year, with CCI referral in anti-competitive cases

q: Compensation under the punitive provisions of ACS-11 is settled by:

options.A: The tender committee
options.B: The General Manager, whose decision is final and conclusive

q: Two-packet tendering is mandatory for works tenders above:

options.A: Rs 5 crore

q: As per MSOP item 5(E), where tender committee members are nominated (not a regular TC), the TC composition/accepting authority is:

options.A: The same as for open tenders
options.C: At least one step higher, except where GM is the accepting authority

q: Contract agreements are signed by an authority:

options.A: One stage above the tender accepting authority
options.B: At the same level as the tender accepting authority
options.D: One stage below the tender accepting authority

q: Under GCC for Services 2018, EMD for works/services estimated to cost up to Rs 1 crore is:

options.A: 2% of the estimated cost

q: Under GCC for Services 2018, EMD for works/services estimated to cost more than Rs 1 crore is:

options.A: 2% of the estimated cost with no maximum
options.D: Rs 2 lakh plus 1/2% of the excess beyond Rs 1 crore, subject to a maximum of Rs 1 crore

q: EMD under GCC for Services is rounded to:

options.A: The nearest Rs 100, like works EMD under ACS-11

q: Which statement about ACS-11 and service contracts is correct?

options.A: ACS-11 amended the EMD provisions of GCC for Services 2018 in the same way as works
options.B: No EMD is required for services at all
options.D: GCC for Services 2018 has NOT been amended by ACS-11; the old two-slab EMD continues for services, unlike works where ACS-11 made it a flat 2%

q: Where the service contractor is registered under GST:

options.A: He is paid excluding GST and the Railway deposits tax under RCM
options.B: He is paid the gross amount including GST and deposits the GST himself

q: TDS under GST on service contract payments is deducted at:
Under MSOP item 44, service contracts can be awarded by:

options.A: PHOD/CHOD with full powers; DRM up to Rs 100 crore per case

q: The DRM's power for service contracts was earlier Rs 20 crore per case and is now:

options.A: Rs 50 crore

q: Where the service contractor is NOT registered under GST:

options.A: He is paid including GST
options.D: He is paid excluding GST and the Railway deposits the tax under reverse charge (RCM)

q: Many service tenders quote rates:

options.A: Inclusive of GST, though this is tender-specific (some are exclusive)
options.B: Always exclusive of GST by law

q: In works contracts, rates are quoted:

options.A: Inclusive of GST in all cases
options.C: Exclusive of GST; GST is paid extra on a valid tax invoice (subject to reflection in the Railways' GSTIN)

q: Under clause 37 of GCC, a post-tender statutory increase in GST is:

options.A: Borne by the contractor
options.C: Reimbursed on proof of payment; a decrease is recovered from bills/SD — GST change is the only rate-escape under 46A.3(a)

q: As per ACS-6 (Board letter dt 21.12.2023), new para 6(a)(v) requires the contractor to:

options.A: Pay/refund the GST collected along with interest and penalties if the Railways' ITC is denied due to wrong invoices, non-filing of returns, non-payment of GST to authorities, or other non-compliance, with a general indemnity for all GST losses
options.C: Pay GST only on the final bill
options.D: Claim ITC on behalf of the Railways

q: On GST non-compliance by the contractor, the Railway may:

options.A: Terminate the contract immediately without notice
options.B: Hold retention money on any GST non-compliance until ITC is verified
options.D: Pay the contractor extra GST as compensation

q: GST on liquidated damages and forfeited EMD/SD is:

options.A: Payable at 18%
options.D: Not applicable — per Board RBA 41/2022 and GST Circular 11/2022 dt 10.08.2022, LD is not consideration for tolerating breach

q: Where LD is recovered from a contractor's bill, the vendor is paid:

options.A: The full bill without any deduction
options.B: The supply value excluding GST, minus LD with GST
options.C: The supply value including GST, minus LD computed without GST

q: As per Railway Board letter No. 2022/R(G)/779/14 dt 10.11.2022:

options.A: Tenderers must give Jurisdictional Assessing Officer details in the bid, and a copy of the LOA/PO is sent to the AO on award
options.B: GST registration is optional for bidders
options.C: LOA copies are never shared with tax authorities
options.D: JAO details are needed only for foreign bidders

q: Railway Board letter No. 2024/RS(G)/779/11 dt 11.09.2025 provides that IRS Conditions of Contract 2025:

options.A: Removes "GST during tender evaluation" from the standard conditions
options.B: Adds GST evaluation as a new standard condition
options.C: Makes GST evaluation mandatory for all stores tenders
options.D: Doubles the GST rate for stores

q: GST 2.0 rate rationalisation came into effect from:
Which statement about tender evaluation and GST is correct?

options.A: Works tenders are evaluated including GST; stores were evaluated excluding GST
options.B: Both are always evaluated including GST
options.C: Works tenders are evaluated excluding GST, while pre-2025 stores tenders were evaluated with GST on an all-inclusive ranking basis
